newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee in downside bias if below $1,890.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee in downside bias if below $1,890.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
Robusta coffee futures need to regain a foothold at $1,890 basis benchmark September if the market is to avoid further falls, technical analysts said on Tuesday.
Traders said the market was due to open unchanged to $10 down.
Elli Gifford, an independent chart analyst, said coffee appeared to have run into some trouble after hitting initial support at $1,775.
The next major support is pegged at $1,695.
"It needs to recover to $1,890 at least to avoid further falls. Otherwise, the original downside objective of $1,695 looks likely to be achieved," she said.
After a five-month frenetic rally since January, June was relatively a calmer month for coffee futures, with prices moving in a tight range between $1,700 and $1,900 for the most of the month.
The market rose from a low of $1,203 in January to peak at $2,700 in late May. Since then, the market had been struggling to stay above $1,800.
But the downside seemed limited now due to a dearth of origin selling notably from Indonesia and the prevailing winter in Brazil.
Brazil's coffee belt had so far escaped crop-damaging frost. But cooler weather was predicted over the weekend, sending New York arabica futures higher on Monday.
"This is the critical time of the year -- the first two weeks of July especially," said one U.S. trader.

In London, spot July enters the month-long delivery period on Tuesday. There have been concerns over the low pass rate for coffee graded under new grading terms which took effect with the July contract onwards. --Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
